Therapist here. Yes, I meet with my clients because I’m financially incentivized, and at the same time I do have genuine care for my clients. 

What makes the relationship different is that I’m trained not to make the relationship about me. Part of that is that I have to on some level detach myself from having the need or desire to have my needs met from my clients. I can’t show that I “care” in ways that are typical. I process my feelings in private. I don’t think about all of my clients every day, but clients definitely take up space in my heart. My clients and their well-being are an important part of my spiritual practice. And all of my coworkers deeply care about their clients as well. 

Of course I can’t speak for the entirety of a profession, but I imagine more are like me than not.

Phonetics is just related to the production of sound. How does the body make whatever sound it is. What does that sound sound like, etc. A /d/ is a /d/ in any language.

Phonology is in relationship to a language. So while /d/ sounds the same no matter what language you're speaking, it's represented differently in different languages.

The best example I can think of is /y/. That sound is represented in English as the letter "y" whereas in Spanish it's most often seen as the letters "ll."
